top_story: A U.S.-Iran confrontation that began with strikes and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz on July 11 has hardened into a broader campaign, with Washington sustaining attacks through a third night on July 13 before launching additional strikes on July 14. As military pressure expanded, the U.S. blockade on Iranian ports and coercive moves around Hormuz pushed the crisis from a bilateral clash toward a regional energy emergency, driving oil prices higher and exposing Gulf states, shipping networks, and civilian economies to immediate risk. Iran has answered with claims of attacks on U.S. military sites in the Gulf and a threat on July 15 to halt all Middle East energy exports, signaling a willingness to widen the economic battlefield even at steep cost to the region. The trajectory now points toward a conflict in which maritime choke points, public livelihoods, and regional stability are becoming the main leverage and the main casualties.
